newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TAC sinks to new 1997 low.
newsitem.headline: TAC sinks to new 1997 low.

text.p: Shares in Thai cellular phone operator Total Access Communications Plc (TAC) fell in Signapore to a 1997 low of US$5.80 in moderately active trading on Thursday.
At 0740 GMT, the stock was down 15 cents to US$5.85. Total volume was 336,400.
Analysts said the stock has been under selling pressure as Thailand's cellular phone market is liberalised.

"The main concern is increasing competition in the sector. In addition, Thai cellular stocks are expensive relative to other cellular stocks in the region," said Gautam Kapoor, regional telecom analyst with ING Barings.
However, Kapoor said he still expected TAC shares to peform relatively well compared with the Thai stock market.
"It should still do well. We expect strong earnings growth of about 20 percent for the next three years from the group."
He said TAC shares had held up relatively well despite the weak Thai stock market. ING Barings has a buy recommendation on TAC.
